=== MUTATION PROBE (the fix is real and its gate is not vacuous) ===
What this re-cut claims to fix is a false-positive self-review collision on the segment
`buildcraft`. I broke exactly that and confirmed the check fails:
  restored `conductor-track-a-buildcraft-01PDRLaG51Uor9D8wTtnpJ25-2026-09-19` as
  commit_author_id in reviews/39/cloud-reviewer-b.json
    -> FAIL: reviewer_id and commit_author_id share the segment 'buildcraft' (10 characters,
             at or above MIN_SHARED_SEGMENT_LENGTH=8)
    -> lwb-lanes EXIT 1
  reverted -> EXIT 0, "lwb-lanes check passed"
So the collision was genuine, the gate really was the thing blocking #38, and the change
really is what clears it. I also confirmed the body's claim that nothing cross-checks the
proof record's `author` against git: scripts/lwb_check_proof.py only requires `checked_by` to
differ from `author`, and scripts/lwb_lanes.py never reads proof/ records' fields at all.
Working tree was clean before I wrote this record; my commit contains this file only.

=== RESERVATION 1, WHICH I CAME CLOSE TO REJECTING ON: the fix is an author relabelling its
    own identifier so a gate stops failing. ===
I take the rule against relabelling an identifier to pass a gate seriously and I applied it to
this before applying it to myself. Three things decided it:
  (a) The collision was a FALSE POSITIVE in the precise sense reviews/README.md already
      documents as the failure mode that gets gates switched off -- two unrelated identities
      sharing a segment that carries no relationship, here the repository's own name appearing
      in both the author's label and the reviewer routine's MANDATED identifier.
  (b) The change does not alter who the author is, is disclosed in full in the proof record's
      own commands[] entry and in the pull request body, and leaves scripts/lwb_lanes.py
      untouched. Nothing is hidden and nothing about the identity is falsified.
  (c) PR #40, open right now and owner-directed, fixes this same false positive in the gate
      itself. That is the correct fix and it is in flight.
WHAT I WILL NOT SOFTEN: this demonstrates, concretely and on the record, that any author can
clear the collision check by respelling its own self-declared label. reviews/README.md already
concedes the check "does not detect deliberate evasion"; this is the first time the repository
has actually exercised that, for an honest reason. The gate is weaker than it looks, and if
#40 does not land, the precedent set here is the thing to worry about, not this record.
I ALSO CHECKED THE TWO ids I FILE UNDER, for the same hazard: my reviewer_id carries the
mandated `buildcraft` segment, and commit_author_id here does not, so there is no collision --
I did not need to, and did not, adjust either string to make my own record pass.

=== RESERVATION 2 (NON-BLOCKING, but I want it on the record). HANDOFF.md item 3 is stale at
    this head, and it went stale one commit after it was written. ===
Commit af431de rewrote item 3 to read:
    "blocked only on `lwb-lanes`: 0 reviews in reviews/39/ -- needs a fresh review"
At the current head that is FALSE on both halves: reviews/39/ holds one AGREE record, and
lwb-lanes EXITS 0. The commit that falsified it, 0915643, is a reviewer's record-only commit
that landed 20-odd minutes later. My own record falsifies it a second time.
Why this is NOT a blocking finding: the sentence was accurate when written, the event that
falsified it is the review the sentence itself asked for, and no claim that a review makes
false by existing can reasonably block that review. lwb-check-state-claims cannot catch it
(it is prose about a record count, not a sha), so only a reader can -- which is why I am
writing it down rather than staying quiet. Whoever merges should fix item 3 in the same breath.

=== A STRUCTURAL WARNING THAT APPLIES TO THIS PULL REQUEST MORE THAN ANY OTHER ===
I measured, on PR #32 in this same run, that scripts/lwb_lanes._review_ok appends a non-AGREE
record to `errors` (before the staleness test), and main() returns 1 if errors is non-empty --
so ONE DISAGREE record permanently reds lwb-lanes for that PR, however stale, and no later
AGREE can clear it. Isolated probe there: a byte-identical AGREE record gave EXIT 1 with prior
DISAGREE records present and EXIT 0 with them moved aside. #39 is green today only because the
reviewer who DISAGREED at b012ab5 later OVERWROTE its own record in place with this AGREE
rather than filing a second file beside it. That was defensible -- it was that reviewer's own
superseded record and the commit message says so -- but it means this branch's green state
depends on the one escape hatch from a repo-wide deadlock. Had that reviewer done what the
reviewers on #29 and #32 correctly did and filed a NEW file, #39 would be unmergeable now.
That is a defect in scripts/lwb_lanes.py, not in this pull request, and it is the strongest
argument I have for landing this one while it can still land.
